payload.task_text:
I need help analyzing quiz performance in the Creative Computing and Culture course from Spring 2014 and setting up support for struggling students.

The quiz submission data for this course has been exported to a CSV file called quiz_submissions.csv in the workspace. Each row contains the quiz title, the quiz's points_possible, and one student's score (a number on a 0-100 scale) for that quiz. You can read this file directly (e.g. with python_execute).

Please analyze this quiz submission data and create an Excel file called Quiz_Performance_Report.xlsx in the workspace. The file should have two sheets. The first sheet called Quiz Stats should show each quiz with columns Quiz_Title, Total_Submissions, Avg_Score rounded to 2 decimal places, Min_Score, Max_Score, and Pass_Rate_Pct rounded to 2 decimal places. Pass_Rate_Pct is defined as 100 times (the number of submissions whose score is greater than half of that quiz's points_possible) divided by (the total number of submissions for that quiz). Note: the score column stores a 0-100 value, and points_possible is the small number shown in quiz_submissions.csv. Sort the rows by Avg_Score ascending. The second sheet called Course Summary should have two columns named Metric and Value with rows for Total_Quizzes, Total_Quiz_Submissions, Overall_Avg_Score rounded to 2 decimal places, Lowest_Avg_Quiz showing the title of the quiz with the lowest average score, and Highest_Avg_Quiz showing the title of the quiz with the highest average score. Overall_Avg_Score is the average score across all quiz submissions combined (not the average of the per-quiz averages). Write all computed values into the workbook as literal numbers (do not write Excel formulas).

After the report, create a Google Form called Quiz Improvement Feedback to gather input from students. Add a required multiple-choice question asking which topic the student finds most challenging, with the options Programming Fundamentals, Data Structures, Algorithms, and User Interface Design. Add a required multiple-choice question asking how confident the student feels about quiz preparation on a scale of 1 to 5, with the response options 1, 2, 3, 4, and 5. Add an optional text question asking what additional resources would help the student.

Schedule three tutoring sessions in the calendar. The first session should be on March 12 2026 from 3pm to 5pm titled CCC Spring 2014 Tutoring Session 1. The second session should be on March 19 2026 from 3pm to 5pm titled CCC Spring 2014 Tutoring Session 2. The third session should be on March 26 2026 from 3pm to 5pm titled CCC Spring 2014 Tutoring Session 3. For the times, 3pm to 5pm means 15:00 to 17:00; you may record these in your session's local timezone or in UTC (either representation is accepted).

Send an email to ccc.instructor@university.edu with the subject Creative Computing Quiz Performance Report summarizing the quiz performance findings and mentioning the tutoring sessions that have been scheduled.

Task-Solving Rationable with Sub-task Decomposition:
To solve this task efficiently, the main agent must complete this compact four-quiz task directly; do not dispatch sub-agents. Resolve the accessible task workspace dynamically and use its quiz_submissions.csv and Quiz_Performance_Report.xlsx paths instead of hard-coded /workspace paths.

Start the CSV read, create_form(title="Quiz Improvement Feedback") exactly once, and the three exact calendar searches natively in parallel. Parse the CSV header quiz_title,points_possible,score and validate complete row/title coverage. For each title retain {points_possible,submission_count,nonnull_score_count,score_sum,score_min,score_max,count_score_gt_half_points}; the pass predicate is strictly score > points_possible/2. Compute the four Quiz Stats rows and five Course Summary values once, with deterministic full-title tie-breaks, and freeze them as one canonical payload.

On the returned formId, sequentially add the exact required challenging-topic multiple choice, confidence multiple choice, and optional resources text question, then call get_form(formId); never retry an ambiguous form creation. For each of the three literal tutoring titles/dates, create only when the exact title and UTC window is absent and read the retained event back. The three event branches are independent and should use native-parallel search/create/read batches.

The main agent is the sole writer of Quiz_Performance_Report.xlsx. Create exactly Quiz Stats and Course Summary in the resolved workspace using the task headers, literal rounded values, and required sort order; read both populated ranges back. Once the canonical metrics exist, run the workbook branch and the Sent-mail lookup for registrar-specified recipient ccc.instructor@university.edu / subject Creative Computing Quiz Performance Report natively in parallel. Read candidates to verify recipients, send once only if absent, and copy the canonical overall/highest/lowest facts plus all three tutoring titles/dates into the body.

Finish only after the CSV controls, workbook, exact form, three UTC events and email all reconcile; do not create diagnostic cells, duplicate side effects or a verification wave.
